title: Porsche Teases Mission S Mid-Engine Halo Car

body_markdown:
While the 911 has long been the brand’s core model and has been selling well so far in 2026, there’s been a void in Porsche’s lineup ever since the 918 Spyder left production 11 years ago. About a month ago, we shared news that Porsche was[mulling over a new sports car model](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/porsche-may-tap-audi-nuvolari-for-918-successor/) , and that they’d decide on production by the end of the summer. Now it’s fall, and it’s become clear that Porsche is planning a new halo model to continue the lineage of its mid-engine Carrera GT and 918 Spyder.


In a video shared on YouTube and Instagram, Porsche has given us the vehicle’s name, but little else. Porsche’s statement was brief: “Welcome Mission S. Our love letter to the sports car.​”


The video offers quick cuts of the Mission S but doesn’t leave us with much to go on. At least we can tell the headlights look more like those on the 918 Spyder and less like the angular, vertical lights on the Mission X concept. There are also a pair of thin, horizontal taillights, which do resemble those found on the Mission X. The rear shot also suggests there’s a prominent center spine on the car—perhaps it serves as a snorkel leading to the airbox. We let the video play through several times and took in a few details, including the overall silhouette, that point to a mid-engine layout, one detail that Porsche has already confirmed. Still, we’re left wanting a whole lot more. Fortunately, Porsche plans to unveil the Mission S in just one more week. We should have a full look and a lot more details—including how much it will differ from its Audi Nuvolari stablemate—on October 15.


The Mission S taillight casts some light on its slim rear wing.
